diagnostic_evidence.quote: The result of Eq. \eqref{eq:Mprod} is real for every $\va,\vb\in \R^n$, if and only if every row of $\matM$ is either real, or is conjugate to exactly one other row of $\matM$.

issues.failure_explanation: The necessity proof concludes that a row of M has a single nonzero entry, which is false for standard complex tubal matrices. The intended argument should concern the row structure of N=overline(M)M^{-1} and then use N_{ij}≠0 to pair rows of M.

failure_location.quote: So, row $i$ of $\matM$ has a single non-zero entry $\matN_{ij}$ for some $j$, and row $i$ and $j$ of $\matM$ are conjugate of each other.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the proof by showing N has one nonzero entry in each row and using N_{ij}≠0 to obtain row j = conjugate row i, or replace it with a valid proof of the characterization.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed iff characterization of invertible complex matrices M for which Mprod is real is unsupported; the restated lemma in the additional proofs is invalid as written.
issues.title: Characterization of real Mprod proof conflates rows of M and N
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the proof argument suffices; the lemma's statement and the surrounding algebraic claims can be preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The same four equation hold if we replace $\va$ with $\matR_\va$, $\vy$ with $\matR_\vy$ and $\Mprod$ with matrix product. Thus, $\matR_\vy$ is the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $\matR_\va$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed conditions replace the required self-adjointness/Penrose conditions by the partial inverse ^pinv, and the construction of vy leaves the zero complex-pair case and an undefined index l. This does not establish that a^winv is real.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the proof with the direct argument that M a has real/conjugate entries, (M a)^pinv preserves that structure, and M^{-1} maps such vectors to real vectors, handling zero pairs by setting coefficients to zero.
issues.overall_effect: The realness lemma and hence the weak-inverse/Penrose lemma for KM are unsupported.
issues.title: Proof of realness of weak inverse uses false equations
issues.why_classification: The lemma statement is locally repairable by a short direct argument; no substantive claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since complex rows in $\matM$ come in pairs, the parity of the realness must be equal to the parity of $n$,
Consider the case \(n=2\). Since \(\R^2\) is isomorphic \(\C\) we can use the multiplication operation defined by complex numbers to get a field:

issues.failure_explanation: For n=2 there are at least two tubal rings: C (realness 0) and the split-complex ring (realness 2), while the formula gives 1. In general the number of admissible realness values with the same parity as n is floor(n/2)+1, not ceil(n/2).

failure_location.quote: thus there are, up to isomorphism, $\lceil \nicefrac{n}{2} \rceil$ tubal rings.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the count to floor(n/2)+1, or state and prove the intended additional restriction that changes the count.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed count of tubal rings up to isomorphism is false for even n.
issues.title: Incorrect count of tubal rings up to isomorphism
issues.why_classification: This is a local counting correction; it does not affect the main algebraic construction.

issues.failure_explanation: T has domain KM^p and codomain KM^m, while T^adj has domain KM^m and codomain KM^p. As written, X is taken in KM^m and Y in KM^p, so T(X) and T^adj(Y) are not well-typed.

failure_location.quote: for all $\matX\in\KM^m$ and $\matY\in\KM^p$ we have $T(\matX)\Mdot\matY=\matX\Mdot T^\adj(\matY)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the types in the definition to X∈KM^p and Y∈KM^m.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of Mprod-adjoint and the proposition stating its representative are ill-formed as written.
issues.title: Mprod-adjoint definition has swapped domains
issues.why_classification: A one-line domain correction restores the intended definition without changing the result.

issues.failure_explanation: The Mdot product is a tube, defined as a sum of row products, whereas U^ha Mprod V is a tensor/matrix. The proof substitutes a false dimensional identity in place of the correct trace/sum formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the proof using the defining sum, e.g. <U,V>=sum_i U_i^* Mprod V_i, or equivalently a trace formula, to verify the adjoint identity.
issues.overall_effect: The proof that A^ha represents the adjoint of left multiplication by A is invalid.
issues.title: Adjoint proof uses false matrix/tube identity
issues.why_classification: The proposition remains true; the proof needs a local correction of the inner-product identity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Construct a SVD decomposition for each frontal slices on its own, collecting the left and right unitary matrices to form \(\hat{\tenU}\) and \(\hat{\tenV}\) respectively

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem requires U and V to lie in KM, i.e. to be real tubes. Facewise unitarity of hat U and hat V alone does not imply their inverse M-transforms are real; the proof omits the necessary choice of SVDs respecting the real/conjugate slice structure.

failure_location.quote: Since, by construction, each frontal slices of \(\hat{\tenU}\) and \(\hat{\tenV}\) are unitary, \(\tenU\) and \(\tenV\) are \(\Mprod\)-unitary.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify the construction to pair conjugate transformed slices and keep real slices real, so that the inverse-transformed U and V lie in R^{m×n}, then conclude Mprod-unitarity.
issues.overall_effect: Existence of Mprod-SVD with tubal real factors is unsupported, affecting rank, norm, and Eckart-Young results that use it.
issues.title: Tubal SVD proof does not establish real tubal factors
issues.why_classification: The missing step is a contained correction to the SVD construction; the theorem statement can be preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: For M=cW with W unitary, the Frobenius norm squared scales by |c|^{-2} under the transform. Therefore the error expressed in transformed singular values must carry factor |c|^{-2}, not |c|^{-1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change |c|^{-1} to |c|^{-2} in the displayed error formula.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative error guarantee for the second Eckart-Young theorem is false when |c|≠1.
issues.title: Second Eckart-Young error formula has wrong scaling
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction restores the correct norm scaling without weakening the result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $S \subseteq \C^{n\times n}$, and assume every matrix $\matA \in S$ is diagonalizable over $\C$. Then, $\matA \matB = \matB \matA$ for all $\matA,\matB\in S$ if and only if there exists a nonsingular $\matS\in \C^{n\times n}$

issues.failure_explanation: As stated, the lemma requires a single invertible S to diagonalize every n×n matrix, which is false. The cited fact and the argument later need only simultaneous diagonalization of the set S.

failure_location.quote: such that, for all $\matA\in\C^{n\times n}$, $\matS\matA\matS^{-1}$ is diagonal.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace A∈C^{n×n} by A∈S in the lemma statement.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of joint diagonalizability of representation matrices, the equivalence proposition, and the main theorem rely on the corrected statement.
issues.title: Simultaneous diagonalization lemma misstated
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and restores the standard simultaneous diagonalization fact used in the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: From x^winv = x^winv x x^winv ∈ (a) one cannot infer x^winv ∈ (a); ideal closure does not allow extracting a factor from a product. The proof therefore does not establish that the principal ideal is von Neumann regular.

failure_location.quote: Since $(\va)$ is an ideal, products on the left and right, even with elements not necessarily from $(\va)$, must be in $(\va)$, so $\vx^\winv\in (\va)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Complete the proof by using the idempotent e_a=a a^winv, showing (a)=(e_a), and verifying that elements of (e_a) have weak inverses inside (e_a).
issues.overall_effect: The claim that principal ideals are tubal sub-rings is unsupported, weakening the decomposition into subfields and the main theorem.
issues.title: Principal ideal subring proof has invalid ideal-closure inference
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is standard and local; the decomposition and main theorem can be preserved once the principal-ideal proof is completed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The use of complex numbers is unavoidable. It can be shown that no such real \(\matM\) exists.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm's contract requires a real matrix M. For the tubal ring isomorphic to C, no real M exists and the correct M is complex; initializing M as real also prevents returning the complex eigendata.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the required and initialized M to C^{n×n} and perform complex arithmetic, or explicitly restrict the algorithm to real-like rings and state that limitation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated guarantee that the algorithm finds M for every tubal ring fails for non-real, e.g. complex, tubal rings.
issues.title: Find-M algorithm requires a real matrix M
issues.why_classification: The construction itself is mostly recoverable; the input-output type must be corrected, which is a local repair.
